title: Analysis of Hematopoietic Lineages in Adult Zebrafish Kidney Marrow
author: Mahony, Monteiro

steps.title: Obtain approvals and prepare reagents
steps.instruction: Secure institutional animal‑experiment permission, follow local zebrafish euthanasia regulations (Schedule 1 killing with Tricaine overdose), obtain flow‑cytometry facility training, and raise adult zebrafish of the desired genotype to ≥3 months post‑fertilization (both sexes unless a specific sex is required). Prepare Tricaine solution (5 g L⁻¹ in Tris‑HCl, pH 7) and PBS/10 % FBS (PBS pH 7.4 with 10 % fetal bovine serum). Label one Eppendorf tube per kidney marrow (or per pooled group) and add 500 µL PBS/10 % FBS; keep tubes on ice.

steps.title: Euthanize and dissect kidney marrow
steps.instruction: Place each adult zebrafish in buffered Tricaine (5 mg mL⁻¹) for ~5 min until movement stops, confirm death by checking cessation of circulation at the tail fin or eye vasculature, then lay the fish on its back on a sponge. Using small scissors, cut the skin from the anus up the belly to just below the gill start; with sharp forceps remove all internal organs without puncturing the heart, and discard any eggs. Peel the whole kidney marrow (WKM) from the dorsal wall with forceps (or scrape with a P1000 tip), taking care not to damage the adjacent large blood vessel. Transfer the WKM into the pre‑labelled tube containing 500 µL PBS/10 % FBS and keep on ice. For cytosmears, retain ~1/3 of the marrow for slide preparation and place the remaining ~2/3 in the tube for flow analysis.

steps.title: Generate single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Using a P1000 non‑filter pipette tip, pipette the WKM in its 500 µL PBS/10 % FBS up/down 5–10 times until the mixture appears cloudy; repeat if large tissue fragments remain. Transfer the suspension to a clean, dry 5 mL polystyrene round‑bottom tube fitted with a 35 µm filter cap (ensure the filter is wet). Add ~100 µL PBS/10 % FBS to the filter, then add the ~500 µL cell suspension and allow it to drip through. Rinse the filter with 500 µL PBS/10 % FBS four times total. Centrifuge the filtrate at 1000 rpm (~300 g) for 5 min at 4 °C; a red pellet (RBCs) should be visible. Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 200 µL PBS/10 % FBS containing Hoechst 33342 diluted 1:10 000 (prepare the Hoechst solution in PBS/10 % FBS beforehand). Keep the suspension on ice in the dark until flow cytometry.

steps.title: Flow cytometry acquisition and analysis
steps.instruction: Optionally count cells with a hemocytometer and stain dead cells with trypan blue (1:10) to estimate total cell numbers. Load samples onto a BD LSRFortessa X‑20 (or equivalent) with BD FACSDiva software. Power on the instrument, allow lasers to warm for ~20 min, and perform routine cleaning. Activate the Hoechst (BV510) laser and any additional fluorophore lasers. Run a first sample, gating out debris (erythrocytes have low FSC), then exclude doublets by plotting FSC‑area vs. FSC‑height. Gate out dead cells (Hoechst‑low). Set FSC on a linear scale and SSC on a log scale, adjusting voltages so most cells fall within the display range. Acquire 10 k–50 k events to resolve the four major populations (erythrocytes, myeloid, progenitors, lymphoid) and adjust gates accordingly. If using multiple fluorophores, include fluorescence‑minus‑one (FMO) controls to define negative thresholds. Optionally sort fluorescently labelled cells on a BD FACSAria Fusion for downstream applications (e.g., scRNA‑seq, scATAC‑seq).

steps.title: May‑Grünwald‑Giemsa staining of smears
steps.instruction: Prepare diluted stains: mix May‑Grünwald (MG) 1:1 with distilled water and Giemsa 1:10 with distilled water. Incubate slides (cytospun cells or WKM smears) in diluted MG for 5 min at 18 °C–22 °C, then wash 5–10 times with distilled water. Incubate in diluted Giemsa for 30 min at 18 °C–22 °C, wash again 5–10 times with distilled water, and air‑dry completely. Mount slides with a small drop of DPX mounting medium and let set for ~16 h. Image the stained slides using a slide scanner or a microscope equipped with a digital camera.

description: In zebrafish, Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) reside in their adult niche, the kidney marrow. Here they self-renew and differentiate to all blood lineages to sustain hematopoiesis.2,3 Marrow failure happens when HSPCs fail to maintain hematopoiesis, often triggering cytopenias, malignant transformation and eventually leukemia.4 To study this process, it is therefore important to characterize the hematopoietic cells in their adult niche. Before you begin, ensure you have sufficient animals of the required genotypes for your analyses and that all the required materials and equipment are ready to use, such as a low magnification stereomicroscope for WKM isolation. See “key resources table” and “materials and equipment” for the lists of these items. This protocol describes the isolation and analysis of WKM by flow cytometry and cellular phenotyping in fish older than 3 months post fertilization (mpf). However, the same protocol could be applied to younger fish (smaller WKM, thus lower cell numbers per animal) or to isolate cells for analysis by single cell genomics (e.g., scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq).
